DAMGHANI:v1p325/r15.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p325/r15.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p325/r15.claim: ʿAẓīm can mean excellent or good, describing the Prophet’s character.
DAMGHANI:v1p325/r15.anchor: العظيم الحسن قوله تعالى في سورة ن

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p425/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p425/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p425/r1.claim: The Prophet’s lofty character, like that of earlier prophets, answers those who dismiss his mission as poetry, soothsaying, or madness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p425/r1.anchor: just as prophets before him had exemplary character, he too, has a lofty character

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p425/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p425/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p425/r2.claim: The Qur’an contrasts the Prophet with poets and soothsayers whose morals, reasoning, and practice are degraded; those grouping him with them are rebuked.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p425/r2.anchor: the moral depletion of poets and soothsayers, their intellectual ramblings and the lack of correspondence between what they claim and what they practice

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r2.claim: Most of the sūra was revealed concerning al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra and Abū Jahl; its opening refutes accusations of madness and praises the Prophet's patience and character.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r2.anchor: ومعظمها نزل في الوليد بن المغيرة وأبي جهل.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r3.claim: The sūra follows a prior account of the blessed and wretched and God's power and knowledge, answering claims that the Prophet's revelation was poetry, magic, or madness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p234/r3.anchor: وكان الكفار ينسبونه مرة إلى الشعر، ومرة إلى السحر، ومرة إلى الجنون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r6.claim: A summary of al-Muntakhab says God's favor removed a blameworthy trait and supplied a praiseworthy one; the Prophet's eloquence, reason, sound character, and virtue demonstrate that his accusers lie.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r6.anchor: وفي المنتخب ما ملخصه المعنى: انتفى عنك الجنون بنعمة ربك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r7.claim: The promise of reward for enduring abuse and inviting people to God means taunts should not deter the Prophet; the great-character verse explains the favor and refutes the charge of madness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p235/r7.anchor: فلا يمنعك ما قالوا عن الدعاء إلى الله. وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p236/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p236/r7.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p236/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid explain the Prophet's great character as a great religion, the dearest religion to God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p236/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد: دين عظيم ليس دين أحب إلى الله تعالى منه.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p236/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p236/r8.speaker: عائشة وعلي وقتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p236/r8.claim: ʿĀʾisha says his character was the Qur'an, ʿAlī calls it Qur'anic etiquette, and Qatāda says it was acting on God's commands.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p236/r8.anchor: وقالت عائشة: إن خلقه كان القرآن. وقال علي: هو أدب القرآن.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p236/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p236/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p236/r9.claim: Another explanation calls the character great because it gathers noble disposition, purity, beautiful temperament, generosity, and responsiveness; he cites prophetic sayings praising good character.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p236/r9.anchor: وقيل: سمي عظيما لاجتماع مكارم الأخلاق فيه،

TABATABAI:68:1-33/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r6.claim: Khuluq is a settled inward disposition from which actions flow easily; it can be praiseworthy virtue or blameworthy vice, though unqualified use means good character.
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r6.anchor: الخلق هو الملكة النفسانية التي تصدر عنها الأفعال بسهولة

TABATABAI:68:1-33/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r7.speaker: الراغب
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r7.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes khuluq, inward dispositions perceived by insight, from khalq, outward forms and shapes perceived by sight.
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r7.anchor: قال الراغب والخلق - بفتح الخاء - والخلق - بضم الخاء - في الأصل واحد

TABATABAI:68:1-33/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r8.claim: In context, the Prophet's great character especially means social virtues: steadfastness, patience with abuse, forgiveness, generosity, gentleness, tact, and humility.
TABATABAI:68:1-33/r8.anchor: ناظرة إلى أخلاقه الجميلة الاجتماعية المتعلقة بالمعاشرة كالثبات على الحق والصبر على أذى الناس

TABATABAI:68:1-33#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#2/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:1-33#2/r7.claim: The claim that great character here means religion or Islam is unsound unless it is referred back to the contextual social virtues just described.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#2/r7.anchor: ومما تقدم يظهر أن ما قيل

TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r8.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r8.claim: Abu Jaʿfar interprets the Prophet's great character as Islam.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r8.anchor: عن أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قول الله عز وجل { وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم } قال هو الإسلام

TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r9.claim: A report in al-Qummi gives the gloss that the Prophet had a great religion.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r9.anchor: في تفسير القمي عن أبي الجارود عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في قوله { وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم } قال على دين عظيم

TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r10.claim: The reports mean that Islam and religion encompass perfected character and that the Prophet followed them.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#4/r10.anchor: يريد اشتمال الدين والإسلام على كمال الخلق واستنانه صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم به

TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r1.speaker: رسول الله
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r1.claim: The Prophet says he was sent to complete noble moral qualities.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r1.anchor: بعثت لأتمم مكارم الأخلاق " وفي المجمع بإسناده

TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r2.claim: Al-Dahhak reports that Quraysh insulted ʿAli after the Prophet honored him; the passage identifies the slanderers as those astray and ʿAli as among the guided.
TABATABAI:68:1-33#5/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك قال لما رأت قريش تقديم النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم عليا وإعظامه له نالوا من علي

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r12.claim: “A tremendous character” means that the Prophet follows the great religion of Islam.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r12.anchor: أي على دين عظيم وهو دين الإسلام عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r13.claim: Character is acquired conduct and manners that become settled in a person, distinct from innate disposition.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r13.anchor: وحقيقة الخلق ما يأخذ به الإنسان نفسه من الآداب وإنما سمي خلقا لأنه يصير كالخلقة فيه

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r14.speaker: الجبائي
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r14.claim: The Prophet's great character includes patience for truth, generosity, sound and gentle judgment, endurance in calling to God, pardon, support for believers, and freedom from envy and greed.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r14.anchor: الصبر على الحق وسعة البذل وتدبير الأمور على مقتضى العقل بالصلاح والرفق والمداراة وتحمل المكاره في الدعاء إلى الله

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r15.speaker: عائشة
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r15.claim: Aisha says the Prophet's character comprised the first ten verses of Sūrat al-Muʾminūn.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r15.anchor: وقالت عائشة: كان خلق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ما تضمنه العشر الأول من سورة المؤمنين

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r16.claim: God's description of the Prophet as possessing tremendous character is the highest possible praise.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r16.anchor: ومن مدحه الله سبحانه بأنه على خلق عظيم فليس وراء مدحه مدح

TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r17.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r17.claim: His character was great because he treated people with fine manners while his heart remained turned toward God.
TABRISI:68:1-16#2/r17.anchor: سمي خلقه عظيما لأنه عاشر الخلق بخلقه وزايلهم بقلبه فكان ظاهره مع الخلق وباطنه مع الحق

TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r1.claim: The Prophet's character was great because he followed God's instruction to pardon, command what is recognized as right, and turn away from the ignorant.
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r1.anchor: خذ العفو وأمر بالعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين

TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r2.claim: His character gathered the noble traits, supported by the Prophetic report that he was sent to perfect noble character.
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r2.anchor: وقيل: سمي خلقه عظيما لاجتماع مكارم الأخلاق فيه ويعضده ما روي عنه

TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r3.claim: The Prophet says that his Lord educated him and perfected his education.

TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r4.claim: Good character lets a believer attain the rank of someone who prays all night and fasts all day.
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r4.anchor: إن المؤمن ليدرك بحسن خلقه درجة قائم الليل وصائم النهار

TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r5.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ reports that nothing weighs more heavily in the balance than good character.
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r5.anchor: وعن أبي الدرداء قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " ما من شيء أثقل في الميزان من خلق حسن "

TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r6.speaker: الرضا علي بن موسى ع
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r6.claim: A report through al-Riḍā and his forefathers says good character certainly leads to Paradise and bad character to Hell.
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r6.anchor: وعن الرضا علي بن موسى ع عن آبائه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r7.claim: Abū Hurayra reports that the most beloved to God have the best manners, while tale-bearers who divide brothers and seek slips are most hated.
TABRISI:68:1-16#3/r7.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r4.claim: The command in 6:90 to follow earlier prophets concerns their distinctive noble traits, not imitative knowledge of God or their different laws.
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r4.anchor: أولئك الذين هدى الله فبهداهم اقتده

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r5.claim: Since each earlier prophet excelled in a particular virtue, following them all gave Muhammad the combined virtues dispersed among them and an exceptional rank.
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r5.anchor: فلما أمر محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام بأن يقتدي بالكل

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r6.claim: The preposition ʿalā conveys mastery: the Prophet stands over and commands these noble traits as a master commands a servant.

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r7.claim: Character is a settled psychic disposition that makes beautiful actions easy; performing such actions and the ease of performing them are distinct.
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r7.anchor: الخلق ملكة نفسانية يسهل على المتصف بها الإتيان بالأفعال الجميلة

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r8.claim: Good character includes avoiding miserliness, stinginess, and anger; kindness in dealings and speech; avoiding estrangement; lenience in contracts; and generosity toward relatives and in-laws.
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r8.anchor: يدخل في حسن الخلق التحرز من الشح والبخل والغضب

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reportedly interpreted the phrase as meaning that the Prophet followed a great religion.
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r9.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس أنه قال معناه

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r10.speaker: الله تعالى
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r10.claim: A report says God told the Prophet that He had created no religion dearer or more pleasing to Him than Islam, which He chose for the Prophet and his community.
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r10.anchor: لم أخلق دينا أحب إلي ولا أرضى عندي من هذا الدين

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r11.claim: Rāzī rejects equating character with religion: religion perfects the theoretical faculty, while character perfects the practical faculty.

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r12.claim: One answer is that khuluq linguistically means habit, whether in cognition or action.
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r12.anchor: الخلق في اللغة هو العادة سواء كان ذلك في إدراك أو في فعل

RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r13.claim: Another answer is that the soul’s effortless readiness for true divine knowledge, and lack of readiness for false beliefs, can also be called character.
RAZI-FULL:v30p71/r13.anchor: فلما كانت الروح القدسية التي له شديدة الاستعداد للمعارف الإلهية الحقة

RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r1.speaker: عائشة
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r1.claim: When Saʿīd ibn Hishām asked about the Prophet’s character, ʿĀʾisha pointed him to the Quran; when asked again, she said his character was the Quran and recited 23:1–10.
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r1.anchor: فإنه كان خلق النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام

RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r2.claim: Rāzī takes ʿĀʾisha’s answer to indicate a soul naturally drawn to the unseen and repelled by bodily pleasures and worldly happiness.
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r2.anchor: نفسه المقدسة كانت بالطبع منجذبة إلى عالم الغيب

RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r3.speaker: عائشة
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r3.claim: Hishām ibn ʿUrwa reports from his father that ʿĀʾisha said no one had better character than the Messenger, who answered anyone from his family or companions, “At your service.”
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r3.anchor: روى هشام بن عروة عن أبيه عن عائشة

RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r4.speaker: أنس
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r4.claim: Anas said he served the Prophet for ten years, and the Prophet never reproached him for an act he did or failed to do.
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r4.anchor: خدمت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عشر سنين

RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r5.claim: God calls the Prophet’s theoretical perfection great in 4:113 and his practical perfection great here; together these encompass the human faculties.
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r5.anchor: وصف ما يرجع إلى قوته النظرية بأنه عظيم

RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r6.claim: The two forms of perfection show that the Prophet’s soul ranked exceptionally high among human souls, nearly like the angels in strength and completeness.
RAZI-FULL:v30p72/r6.anchor: فلم يبق للإنسان بعد هاتين القوتين شيء

STUDYQURAN:68:4/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r1.speaker: IK, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r1.claim: Some interpret “exalted character” as describing the religion of Islam.
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r1.anchor: Some interpret exalted character as a descriptor of the religion of Islam (IK, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:68:4/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r2.claim: Most understand the verse as describing the Prophet, whose character was exalted because his only aspiration was God.
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r2.anchor: but most associate it with the Prophet himself; his character is said to be exalted because he had no aspiration other than God (Q)

STUDYQURAN:68:4/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r3.speaker: ʿĀʾishah
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r3.claim: Asked about the Prophet’s character, ʿĀʾishah said that his character was the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r3.anchor: The Prophet’s wife ʿĀʾishah was once asked about the Prophet’s character and responded, “Do you not read the Quran? . . . His character was the Quran”

STUDYQURAN:68:4/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r4.claim: Khuluq, “character,” is closely related to khalq, the Quran’s primary word for “creation.”
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r4.anchor: Character translates khuluq, which is closely related to the primary Quranic word for “creation”

STUDYQURAN:68:4/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r5.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r5.claim: The Prophet prayed that God beautify his character as God had beautified his created form.
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r5.anchor: it is reported that the Prophet used to pray, “O God you have beautified my created form

STUDYQURAN:68:4/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r6.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r6.claim: The Prophet said that his mission was to perfect noble character traits.
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r6.anchor: Another ḥadīth states, “I was only sent to perfect the noble traits of character”

STUDYQURAN:68:4/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r7.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r7.claim: The Prophet taught that the best people are those with the best character traits.
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r7.anchor: The Prophet is also reported to have enjoined good character traits upon his followers, saying, “The best of you are those who are best in character

STUDYQURAN:68:4/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r8.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r8.claim: The Prophet enjoined reverence of God, following bad deeds with good ones, and treating people with good character.
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r8.anchor: The Prophet is also reported to have enjoined good character traits upon his followers

STUDYQURAN:68:4/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r9.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r9.claim: The Prophet said that beauty of character is what most admits people into Paradise.
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r9.anchor: “What admits people most into Paradise is beauty of character”

STUDYQURAN:68:4/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r10.speaker: Prophet
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r10.claim: The Prophet said good character weighs heavily on a believer’s scales and can raise one to the rank of those who pray and fast.
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r10.anchor: “Nothing is placed on the scales of a believer that is weightier than beauty of character; and one who has beauty of character will reach thereby the degree of one who prays and fasts”

STUDYQURAN:68:4/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r11.claim: Beautiful character can be understood as the opposite of the state of being possessed mentioned in verse 2.
STUDYQURAN:68:4/r11.anchor: those with beautiful character traits are far from the state of being possessed referred to in verse 2 (Āl)

TAB-FULL:v23p151/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the Prophet's great character as a great religion, specifically Islam in one report.
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r1.anchor: ابن عباس، قوله: {وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم} [القلم: 4] يقول: دين عظيم

TAB-FULL:v23p151/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r2.claim: Mujahid likewise interprets the great character as religion.
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {خلق عظيم} [القلم: 4] قال: الدين

TAB-FULL:v23p151/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r3.speaker: عائشة
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r3.claim: Aisha says the Prophet's character was the Qur'an; reports quote her directing questioners to the Qur'an and this verse.
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r3.anchor: فسألتها عن خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت كان خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم القرآن

TAB-FULL:v23p151/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r4.speaker: عطية
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r4.claim: Atiyya explains the Prophet's great character as the Qur'an's cultivated manners.
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r4.anchor: عن عطية، في قوله: {وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم} [القلم: 4] قال: أدب القرآن

TAB-FULL:v23p151/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd also glosses the phrase as a great religion.
TAB-FULL:v23p151/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم} [القلم: 4] قال: على دين عظيم

TAB-FULL:v23p152/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p152/r1.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v23p152/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak says it is the Prophet's religion and the whole affair he followed among what God commanded and entrusted to him.
TAB-FULL:v23p152/r1.anchor: قال: سمعت الضحاك، يقول، في قوله: {لعلى خلق عظيم} [القلم: 4] يعني دينه، وأمره

THALABI:v10p8/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r13.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
THALABI:v10p8/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say the Prophet possessed a great religion.
THALABI:v10p8/r13.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد: دين عظيم

THALABI:v10p8/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r14.speaker: الحسن
THALABI:v10p8/r14.claim: Al-Hasan says the Prophet's character consisted of the manners of the Qur'an.
THALABI:v10p8/r14.anchor: وقال الحسن: كان خلقه آداب القرآن

THALABI:v10p8/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r15.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v10p8/r15.claim: Aisha describes the Prophet's character as the Qur'an.
THALABI:v10p8/r15.anchor: ونقلت عائشة عن خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ورضي عنها فقالت: كان خلقه القرآن

THALABI:v10p8/r16.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r16.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v10p8/r16.claim: Qatada says the Prophet's character was to carry out God's commands and avoid His prohibitions.
THALABI:v10p8/r16.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو ما كان يأتمر به من أمر الله وينتهي عنه من نهي الله

THALABI:v10p8/r17.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r17.speaker: جنيد
THALABI:v10p8/r17.claim: Junayd says the Prophet's character was called great because his only aspiration was God.
THALABI:v10p8/r17.anchor: وقال جنيد: سمي خلقه عظيما لأنه لم يكن له همة سوى الله

THALABI:v10p8/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p8/r18.speaker: الواسطي
THALABI:v10p8/r18.claim: Al-Wasiti says the Prophet gave up both worlds in exchange for the Real.
THALABI:v10p8/r18.anchor: وقال الواسطي: لأنه جاد بالكونين عوضا عن الحق

THALABI:v10p10/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p10/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p10/r1.claim: The Prophet's outward bearing was with people, while his heart was inwardly oriented toward God.
THALABI:v10p10/r1.anchor: فكان ظاهره مع الخلق وباطنه مع الحق

THALABI:v10p10/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p10/r2.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
THALABI:v10p10/r2.claim: One explanation says his outward character kept company with people while his heart inwardly turned toward God.
THALABI:v10p10/r2.anchor: بقلبه، فكان ظاهره مع الخلق وباطنه مع الحق

THALABI:v10p10/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p10/r3.speaker: بعض الحكماء
THALABI:v10p10/r3.claim: A sage advises being true with people and sincere with God, matching the distinction between outward dealings and inward devotion.
THALABI:v10p10/r3.anchor: وأوصى بعض الحكماء رجلا فقال: عليك بالحق مع الخلق والصدق مع الحق

THALABI:v10p10/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p10/r4.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
THALABI:v10p10/r4.claim: Another explanation links the Prophet's character to his carrying out God's command to take the forgiving course.
THALABI:v10p10/r4.anchor: وقيل: لأنه امتثل بالدنيا لله تعالى إياه بقوله: خذ العفو الآية

THALABI:v10p10/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p10/r5.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
THALABI:v10p10/r5.claim: One explanation says God magnified the Prophet's character by making colors small in his sight so that he could recognize their Creator.
THALABI:v10p10/r5.anchor: وقيل: عظم له خلقه حيث صغر الألوان في عينه ليعرف لهذه مكونها

THALABI:v10p10/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p10/r6.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
THALABI:v10p10/r6.claim: Another explanation says the Prophet's character was great because it gathered all noble qualities.
THALABI:v10p10/r6.anchor: وقيل: سمي خلقه عظيما لاجتماع مكارم الأخلاق فيه

THALABI:v10p10/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p10/r7.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v10p10/r7.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying he was sent to complete the noble qualities of character.
THALABI:v10p10/r7.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «بعثت لأتمم مكارم الأخلاق»

THALABI:v10p10/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p10/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v10p10/r8.claim: A saying attributed to the Prophet states that his Lord educated him and made his education excellent.

THALABI:v10p10/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p10/r9.speaker: عائشة
THALABI:v10p10/r9.claim: Aisha reports the Prophet saying good character lets a believer attain the rank of one who prays all night and fasts by day.
THALABI:v10p10/r9.anchor: عن عائشة- رضي الله عنها- قالت: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: «إن المؤمن ليدرك بحسن خلقه درجة قائم الليل صائم النهار»

THALABI:v10p10/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p10/r10.speaker: أبو الدرداء
THALABI:v10p10/r10.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the Prophet saying that nothing weighs more heavily in the balance than good character.
THALABI:v10p10/r10.anchor: عن أم الدرداء عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «ما شيء أثقل في الميزان من خلق حسن»

THALABI:v10p10#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p10#2/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
THALABI:v10p10#2/r1.claim: Ali reports the Prophet saying good character certainly leads to Paradise and bad character certainly leads to the Fire.
THALABI:v10p10#2/r1.anchor: «عليكم بحسن الخلق فإن حسن الخلق في الجنة لا محالة، وإياكم وسوء الخلق فإن سوء الخلق في النار لا محالة»

THALABI:v10p10#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p10#2/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
THALABI:v10p10#2/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet loves most those of best character who are easy to live with and both love and are loved; He dislikes gossips who divide brothers and seek others' failings.
THALABI:v10p10#2/r2.anchor: عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أحبكم إلى الله أحسنكم أخلاقا الموطئون أكنافا الذين يألفون ويؤلفون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p75/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p75/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p75/r1.claim: The author introduces the verse as praise of the Prophet accompanied by a promise of reward.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p75/r1.anchor: ثم مدحه مع وعد الأجر بقوله: {وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم}

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:4-15/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:4-15/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:4-15/r1.claim: Muhammad follows the character God commanded in the Qur’an.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:68:4-15/r1.anchor: أنت على الخلق الذي أمرك الله به في القرآن

QASHANI:68:2-4/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:68:2-4/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:68:2-4/r4.claim: His great character comes from embodying God's qualities and receiving holy support; he endures slander and injury through God, not his own strength.
QASHANI:68:2-4/r4.anchor: لكونك متخلقا بأخلاق الله متأيدا بالتأييد القدسي فلا تتأثر بمفترياتهم

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r4.claim: Because the address is specifically to Muḥammad, recipient of divine favor and noble character, who neither read nor wrote before revelation nor knew the Book (29:48; 42:52), Elmalılı prefers the divine primordial Pen, also called the First or Highest Pen; he finds this view in Ibn Jarīr and al-Jalālayn.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r4.anchor: Fakat burada hitab bilhassa ni‘met-i ilâhiyeye mazhar kılınarak, وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍۢ [el-Kalem 68/4] buyurulan zât-ı Hazret-i Muhammedî’ye ait olması

ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r8.claim: The following denial of madness, affirmation of divine favor, understanding, character, and great reward, and condemnation of immoral liars clarify which side of the pen’s significance is praised.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#5/r8.anchor: Bundan dolayı burada bu kasemin arkasından cünûnun, fitnenin nefyi ve ni‘met-i rabbâniyenin idrak ve ahlâkın, ecrin büyüklüğünü beyan ve ahlâksızların, yalancıların zemmi ile o cihete de tenbih buyurulacaktır

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r10.claim: The Prophet was created with very great dispositions, virtues, and spiritual qualities that lead through action toward the highest good; he will attain that goal by following them.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r10.anchor: pek büyük huylar, hakikaten tazime lâyık seciye ve meleke ve mâneviyat üzere yaratılmış bulunuyorsun. Onunla yürüyecek o gayeye ereceksin

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r11.claim: This great character is the straight path and true religion of Islam, formed by Qur'anic etiquette and divine ethics bestowed by God; the Prophet is the believers' good example.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r11.anchor: İşte o ahlâk sırât-ı müstakīmi, dîn-i hak olan dîn-i İslâm’ı teşkil eden

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r12.claim: People fail to grasp the greatness of this character and commit follies that require patience and endurance.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r12.anchor: Onun büyüklüğünü halk idrak edemez de sabr u tahammül edilmesi iktizâ eden deliliklerde bulunurlar

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r13.speaker: Râgıb
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r13.claim: Al-Raghib says khalq and khuluq share an origin like sharb/shurb and sarm/surm; with fatḥ khalq is the visible form, while with ḍamm khuluq is a faculty perceived by the heart.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r14.claim: Khuluq has plurals huluk and akhlaq; in Turkish akhlaq is commonly used as a singular, like evlad.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r14.anchor: Fakat lisânımızda “ahlâk” kelimesinin de “evlâd” kelimesi gibi müfred makamında

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r15.claim: Character denotes settled dispositions; depending on whether one habitually follows good or evil, one distinguishes praiseworthy and blameworthy character.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r15.anchor: meleke ve rüsuh esas olduğundan hayır veya şerri itiyad etmiş olmasına nazaran ahlâk-ı hasene ve ahlâk-ı seyyie

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as a great religion, specifically Islam.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r16.anchor: İbn Abbas’tan: 1. Azîm bir din, 2. Azîm bir din ki o İslâm’dır

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r17.speaker: Mücâhid
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r17.claim: Mujahid explains the Prophet's great character as religion.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r17.anchor: Mücâhid’den: Din. İbn Zeyd’den; edeb-i Kur’an

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r18.speaker: İbn Zeyd
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r18.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the Prophet's character as Qur'anic etiquette.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r18.anchor: Mücâhid’den: Din. İbn Zeyd’den; edeb-i Kur’an

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r19.speaker: عائشة
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r19.claim: Sa'id b. Hisham reports asking Aisha about the Prophet's character; she answered that his character was the Qur'an.

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r20.claim: One sense of Aisha's answer is that the Prophet embodied all the Qur'an's noble qualities and was protected from its condemned defects, fully exemplifying Hud 11:112.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r20.anchor: Kur’an’daki büyük mekârim-i ahlâkın hepsi onda vardı

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r21.claim: Understanding this first sense fully requires understanding the Qur'an in its entirety.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r21.anchor: Onu anlamak Kur’ân’ı tamamen anlamaya mütevakkıftır

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r22.claim: A second sense is that the Prophet's character was so great that no other description could adequately express it.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r22.anchor: öyle büyük bir ahlâk idi ki onu başka bir târif ile anlatmak kābil değildir demek olur

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r23.speaker: ضحاك
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r23.claim: Al-Dahhak says this is the religion and command God ordered the Prophet and entrusted him to uphold.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r23.anchor: Dahhâk’tan لَعَلَىٰ خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍۢ yani Allah’ın ona emrettiği ve onu müvekkel kıldığı dini ve emri

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r24.claim: The tanwin of khuluq magnifies the quality: the Prophet's character has beauties others cannot fully comprehend.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r24.anchor: Burada خُلُقٍ’daki tenvin tefhıym içindir ki sâirlerinin hakkıyla idrak edemeyecekleri güzelliklerle mümtaz bir ahlâk demektir

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r25.claim: The emphatic inna, initial lām, magnifying tanwin, and adjective azim multiply assurances of the Prophet's lofty character; the clause also reinforces the preceding oath response.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r25.anchor: azamet ü ulviyeti kat kat te’mînât içinde beyan ve tebliğ buyurulmuş

ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r26.speaker: author
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r26.claim: Elmalılı presents the verse as a distinguished great sign among the lines written by the Supreme Pen in the clear Book.
ELMALILI:68:1-6#6/r26.anchor: bu Kitâb-ı Mübîn’de Kalem-i A‘lâ’nın yazdığı satırların azîm bir âyet-i mümtâzesi olmak üzere konulmuştur

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r12.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r12.claim: The Prophet's “great character” is his Qur'anic character.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r12.anchor: 4. âyetteki “üstün ahlâk” ise Hz. Peygamber’in sahip olduğu Kur’an ahlâkıdır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r13.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r13.speaker: Hz. Âişe
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r13.claim: Aisha said, in response to a question, that the Prophet's character was the Qur'an's character.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r13.anchor: Hz. Âişe bir soru münasebetiyle Hz. Peygamber’in ahlâkının Kur’an ahlâkı olduğunu belirtmiş

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r14.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r14.speaker: Resûlullah
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r14.claim: The Prophet said he was sent to perfect noble character.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r14.anchor: kendisi de güzel ahlâkı tamamlamak için gönderildiğini ifade buyurmuşlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r15.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r15.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r15.claim: Together these verses present the Prophet as divinely favored, exemplary in character, a model leader for humanity, and a trustworthy guide, contrary to the polytheists' charge of madness.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:68:1/r15.anchor: Allah’ın lutfuna mazhar olmuş yüksek bir şahsiyete ve üstün bir ahlâka sahip, her yönüyle mükemmel

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r10.claim: As God taught Muhammad the histories of earlier prophets, He informed him that their scattered virtues were all gathered in him.
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r10.anchor: عرفه أنه اجتمعت فيه متفرقات أخلاقهم

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r11.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r11.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r11.claim: A report says he refused the keys of the earth and, on the night journey, saw the kingdom and paradise without looking toward them, as 53:17 says.
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r11.anchor: إنه عرض مفاتيح الأرض فلم يقبلها ، ورقاه ليلة المعراج ، وأراه جميع المملكة والجنة فلم يلتفت إليها

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r12.claim: Neither adversity turns him away nor gifts divert him; he endured injury and prayed for his people, and while others will say 'myself,' he will plead for his community.
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r12.anchor: لا بالبلاء تنحرف ، ولا بالعطاء تنصرف ؛ احتمل صلوات الله عليه في الأذى شج رأسه وثغره

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r13.claim: Muhammad says 'my community, my community' when everyone else says 'myself, myself.'
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r13.anchor: وغدا كل يقول : نفسي نفسي وهو صلوات الله عليه يقول : ( أمتي أمتي )

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r14.claim: God taught him fine character through 7:199; Gabriel explained this as keeping ties with one who cuts them, giving to one who withholds, and forgiving one who wrongs.
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r14.anchor: علمه محاسن الأخلاق بقوله : { خذ العفو وأمر بالمعرف وأعرض عن الجاهلين }

QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r15.claim: Asked what his Lord commanded, Muhammad was told to embody fine character: keep ties with those who sever them, give to those who deny him, and pardon wrongdoers.
QUSHAYRI:v3p341/r15.anchor: بماذا يأمرني ربي ؟ قال : يأمرك بمحاسن الأخلاق ؛ يقول لك : صل من قطعك وأعط من حرمك واعف عمن ظلمك

ITQAN:v2p499/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p499/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p499/r1.claim: The non-governing lām of initiation emphasizes a clause and shifts away from sentence-initial position after inna to avoid two successive emphatics; it also makes the imperfect refer to the present.
ITQAN:v2p499/r1.anchor: لام الابتداء وفائدتها أمران توكيد مضمون الجملة ولهذا زحلقوها في باب إن عن صدر الجملة

ITQAN:v2p499/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p499/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p499/r2.claim: The lām of initiation appears with a subject, in predicates of inna, and in its delayed noun construction; examples include لأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ رَهْبَةً, إِنَّ رَبِّي لَسَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ, and إِنَّ لَنَا لَلْآخِرَةَ.
ITQAN:v2p499/r2.anchor: وتدخل في المبتدأ نحو ﴿ لأنتم أشد رهبة ﴾ وفي خبر إن نحو ﴿ إن ربي لسميع الدعاء ﴾

ITQAN:v4p328/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p328/r1.speaker: البارزي
ITQAN:v4p328/r1.claim: Al-Barizi says eloquence chooses the most fitting words for each part of a sentence; humans cannot usually summon every meaning and matching expression, while this is present in God’s knowledge, making the Quran the finest and most eloquent speech.
ITQAN:v4p328/r1.anchor: قال البارزي في أول كتابه ( أنوار التحصيل في أسرار التنزيل ) اعلم أن المعنى الواحد قد يخبر عنه

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r1.speaker: سهل
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r1.claim: The Prophet was disciplined by the Quran and did not cross its limits, as in God’s command to justice and excellence.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r1.anchor: قال سهل : تأدبت بأدب القرآن ولم تتجاوز حدوده وهو قوله : ﴿ إن الله يأمر بالعدل والإحسان

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r2.claim: The Prophet gave up the two worlds in exchange for the Real.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r2.anchor: قال الواسطي : إنه جاد بالكونين عوضا عن الحق

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r3.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r3.claim: His great character meant neither disputing nor being drawn into dispute, through the intensity of his knowledge of God on the Night Journey.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r3.anchor: وقال أيضا : الخلق العظيم أن لا يخاصم ولا يخاصم من شدة معرفته بربه في ليلة المسرى

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r4.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r4.claim: He sees things through the Real’s witnessing rather than his own, since one who sees through himself is ruined.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r4.anchor: قال الحسين : لأنك تنظر إلى الأشياء بشاهد الحق ولا تنظر إلى الأشياء بشاهدك

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r5.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r5.claim: His character is tied to the sweetness of beholding that God grants within his secret.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r5.anchor: وقال الواسطي : لوجدانك حلاوة المطالعة على سرك

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r6.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r6.claim: God fashioned the Prophet upon great character after granting him forms of favor surpassing those received by other prophets and messengers.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r6.anchor: وقال أيضا : إنك قبلت فنون اسديت إليك من نعمي احسن مما قبله غيرك من الأنبياء والرسل

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r7.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r7.claim: After beholding the Real, the harshness of other people no longer affected the Prophet.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r7.anchor: وقال الحسين : معناه أنه لم يؤثر فيك جفاء الخلق بعد مطالعة الحق

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r8.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r8.claim: After seeing the hidden reality of the cosmos, its created forms became small in the Prophet’s sight.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r8.anchor: وقال الحسين : معناه أنه لم يؤثر فيك جفاء الخلق بعد مطالعة الحق . وقال : صغرت الأكوان في عينك

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r9.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r9.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAtaʾ says the Prophet gave up this world and the next in exchange for God.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في قوله : ﴿ وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم ﴾ قال : جدت بالدنيا والآخرة عوضا منا

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r10.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r10.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r10.claim: Junayd says the Prophet bore affliction for God and prayed, “O God, forgive my people, for they do not know.”
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r10.anchor: وقال الجنيد : احتمل في الله البلاء وقال : ' اللهم اغفر لقومي فإنهم لا يعلمون ' .

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r11.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r11.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r11.claim: The created cosmos left no effect upon the Prophet.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r11.anchor: وقال القاسم : ليس للكون عليه أثر

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r12.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r12.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r12.claim: God manifested power through Jesus, efficacy through Asif, and wrath through Moses’s staff, while showing His attributes in Muhammad; ultimately these are qualities of the One described, not another.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r12.anchor: وقال الواسطي : اظهر الله قدرته في عيسى ونفاذه في آصف وسخطه في عصى موسى

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r13.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r13.speaker: فارس
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r13.claim: One of great character devotes himself wholly, then is veiled after having been present.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r13.anchor: وقال فارس : من عظم خلقه كان يتبتل إليه تبتيلا فغيبه بعد الحضور

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r14.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r14.speaker: يحيى بن معاذ
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r14.claim: The exaltation of character contains treasures of provision.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r14.anchor: وقال يحيى بن معاذ : في علو الأخلاق كنوز الأرزاق

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r15.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r15.speaker: أبو سعيد الخراز
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r15.claim: The person of great character has no concern apart from God.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r15.anchor: قال أبو سعيد الخراز في ذلك : ليست لك همة إلا الله

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r16.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r16.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r16.claim: The Prophet’s secret was adorned with the lights of divine character; whoever receives this third direct communion is rightly favored above creation.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r16.anchor: قال الواسطي : كيف لا يكون كذلك من يحلى الله سره بأنوار أخلاقه وحق لمن وقعت له المباشرة الثالثة

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r17.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r17.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r17.claim: Great character is the essence of faith and the reality of divine oneness.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r17.anchor: قال جعفر : هو صرف الإيمان وحقيقة التوحيد

SULAMI:v2p343#3/r18.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r18.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r18.claim: Ordinary people cannot bear this character; it belongs to those who take on divine character. Since God called Himself patient and told David to take on His character, this is the greatest station: stations bind one to common people, but character binds one to divine attributes.
SULAMI:v2p343#3/r18.anchor: وقال الواسطي : الخلق لا يحتمله العام والخلق لمن تخلق لأن الله أوحى إلى داود صلى الله عليه وسلم أن تخلق بأخلاقي

SULAMI:v2p344/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p344/r1.speaker: محمد بن علي الترمذي
SULAMI:v2p344/r1.claim: The Prophet’s greatest character is his abandonment of his own will.
SULAMI:v2p344/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن علي الترمذي : أي خلق اعظم من خلق خص به نبيه وحبيبه وهو ترك مشيئته

SULAMI:v2p344/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p344/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v2p344/r2.claim: Junayd gathers the Prophet’s virtues into generosity, dignity, sincere counsel, and compassion.
SULAMI:v2p344/r2.anchor: وقال الجنيد : وخلق اجمع في أربعة أشياء في السخاوة والأنفة والنصيحة والشفقة

SULAMI:v2p344/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p344/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p344/r3.claim: Great character means having no independent choice, submitting to divine decree and forgiveness, with the self and familiar attachments annihilated.
SULAMI:v2p344/r3.anchor: سمعت ابن عطاء يقول في قوله : ﴿ وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم ﴾ الخلق العظيم أن لا يكون له اختيار ويكون تحت الحكم

SULAMI:v2p344/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p344/r4.speaker: أبو سعيد القرشي
SULAMI:v2p344/r4.claim: The Great is God, whose attributes include generosity, forbearance, forgiveness, and excellence; the Prophet adopted his Lord’s character. A prophetic report says God has more than one hundred character traits and whoever has one enters Paradise.
SULAMI:v2p344/r4.anchor: قال أبو سعيد القرشي : العظيم هو الله ومن اخلاقه الجود والكرم والصفح والعفو والإحسان الا ترى إلى ما روى عن النبي

SULAMI:v2p344/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p344/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد
SULAMI:v2p344/r5.claim: God magnified the Prophet by adorning him with this character.
SULAMI:v2p344/r5.anchor: وقال أبو سعيد : عظمه حيث زينه به

SULAMI:v2p344/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p344/r6.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p344/r6.claim: The Prophet moved beyond moral attributes toward the divine Essence, then was annihilated through the Essence until reaching its reality; one who passes away from annihilation is replaced by another who abides.
SULAMI:v2p344/r6.anchor: وقال الحسين : عظم خلقك حيث لم ترض بالأخلاق وسرت ولم تسكن إلى النعوت حتى وصلت إلى الذات

SULAMI:v2p344/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p344/r7.speaker: الحسين
SULAMI:v2p344/r7.claim: His secret is great because God adorned it with the lights of His character; the person granted the third direct communion is favored among creation.
SULAMI:v2p344/r7.anchor: وقال الحسين : كيف لا يكون سره عظيما وقد حلى الله سره بأنوار اخلاقه وحق له لمن وفقت له المباشرة الثالثة

SULAMI:v2p344/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p344/r8.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p344/r8.claim: Sent in the Hijaz, the Prophet was kept from pleasures and desires and exposed to estrangement and hardship; after this purified him from moral blemish, God called his character great.
SULAMI:v2p344/r8.anchor: قال الواسطي : لما بعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالحجاز حجبه بها عن اللذات والشهوات وألقاه في الغربة والجفوة

TUSTARI:68:4/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:68:4/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:68:4/r1.claim: The Prophet's character followed the Quran and never crossed its limits, including God's command to justice and excellence in 16:90.
TUSTARI:68:4/r1.anchor: تأدبت بأدب القرآن، فلم تتجاوز حدوده وهو قوله تعالى:

TUSTARI:68:4/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:68:4/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:68:4/r2.claim: Anger and harshness arise from relying on one's own strength; leaving that reliance allows inner weakness to produce mercy and gentleness, embodying God's qualities.
TUSTARI:68:4/r2.anchor: إن الغضب والحدة من سكون العبد إلى قوته، فإذا خرج من سكونه إلى قوته

TUSTARI:68:4/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:68:4/r3.speaker: author
TUSTARI:68:4/r3.claim: The Prophet's gentleness toward people is also exemplified in 3:159.
TUSTARI:68:4/r3.anchor: وقال: فبما رحمة من الله لنت لهم

TUSTARI:68:4/r4.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:68:4/r4.speaker: الله
TUSTARI:68:4/r4.claim: God tells David to take on His qualities, saying that He is patient.
TUSTARI:68:4/r4.anchor: وقد أوحى الله تعالى إلى داود عليه السلام فقال: " تخلق بأخلاقي فإني أنا الصبور

TUSTARI:68:4/r5.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:68:4/r5.speaker: author
TUSTARI:68:4/r5.claim: Good character is the greatest spiritual station: lesser stations connect with ordinary people, while noble character connects with divine attributes.
TUSTARI:68:4/r5.anchor: فمن أوتي الخلق الحسن فقد أوتي أعظم المقامات، لأن ما دونه من المقامات ارتباط بالعامة

TUSTARI:68:4/r6.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:68:4/r6.speaker: author
TUSTARI:68:4/r6.claim: Sahl calls changing a blameworthy trait into a praiseworthy one the greatest spiritual gift; other marvels soon pass.
TUSTARI:68:4/r6.anchor: ولكن أكبر الكرامات أن تبدل خلقا مذموما من أخلاقك بخلق محمود

SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p218#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p218#2/r2.speaker: عائشة
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p218#2/r2.claim: Aisha says no one had better character than the Prophet: whenever a Companion or family member called him, he answered, “At your service”; this occasioned the verse.
SUYUTI-LUBAB:v1p218#2/r2.anchor: عن عائشة قالت ما كان أحد أحسن خلقا من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما دعاه أحد

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p443/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p443/r1.speaker: عائشة
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p443/r1.claim: Aisha says no one had better character than the Prophet, who always answered a summons from a companion or family member with labbayk; this prompted the verse.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p443/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: ما كان أحد أحسن خلقا من رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - ما دعاه أحد

DAMGHANI:v1p332/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r4.claim: ʿAlā can mean that something belongs to or is inherent in someone: the Prophet possesses magnificent character; 39:22 is grouped with it.
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r4.anchor: على بمعنى له قوله سبحانه في سورة ن وانك لعلى خلق عظيم

FARRA:v3p172/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p172/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p172/r4.claim: خلق عظيم means a great religion.

NAHHAS:v5p5/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p5/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p5/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the Prophet's great character as his religion.
NAHHAS:v5p5/r8.anchor: روى ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس قال على دين

NAHHAS:v5p5/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p5/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p5/r9.claim: On this reading, character means good religion, way, doctrine, and obedience, like the saying that the best believers have the best character.
NAHHAS:v5p5/r9.anchor: فيكون هذا مثل قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم أكمل المؤمنين إيمانا أحسنهم خلقا أي أحسنهم دينا

NAHHAS:v5p5/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p5/r10.speaker: عائشة
NAHHAS:v5p5/r10.claim: Asked about the Prophet's great character, ʿĀʾisha answered: the Qur'an.
NAHHAS:v5p5/r10.anchor: وسئلت عائشة رضي الله عنها ما الخلق العظيم الذي كان عليه قالت القرآن

NAHHAS:v5p5/r11.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p5/r11.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p5/r11.claim: Another view is that it means his cheerfulness, meeting people's needs, honoring them, and gentleness.
NAHHAS:v5p5/r11.anchor: وقيل هو ما كان فيه من البشاشة والسعي في قضاء حاجات الناس وإكرامهم والرفق بهم

ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r6.claim: Two reported interpretations gloss the great character as Islam or as the Qur'an.
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r6.anchor: قيل: على الإسلام، وقيل: على القرآن

ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r7.claim: Zajjāj's preferred explanation is that the Prophet follows the character God commanded in the Qur'an.
ZAJJAJ:v5p203#2/r7.anchor: والمعنى - والله أعلم - أنت على الخلق الذي أمرك الله به في القرآن

ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n4/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n4/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n4/r1.claim: Khuluq can mean character, innate disposition or nature, as well as habitual behavior that becomes second nature (Taj al-'Arus).
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n4/r1.anchor: The term khuluq, rendered by me as "way of life", describes a person's "character", "innate disposition" or "nature"

ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n4/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n4/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n4/r2.claim: Asad renders khuluq as 'way of life', following Ibn Abbas's equation with din and the latter's primary sense of a way or manner of acting.
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n4/r2.anchor: explanation of the above verse by Abd Allah ibn Abbas (as quoted by Tabari), stating that this term is here synonymous with din

ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n4/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n4/r3.speaker: A'ishah
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n4/r3.claim: In well-authenticated traditions, A'ishah repeatedly said of Muhammad that his way of life was the Qur'an; Asad lists reports transmitted through several authorities and compilations.
ASAD-NOTES:68:1#n4/r3.anchor: his way of life (khuluq) was the Qur'an." (Muslim, Tabari and Hakim, on the authority of Said ibn Hisham

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r1.claim: The opening verses affirm the Prophet’s mission and steady him against deniers who dispute the miracle and claim the Qur’an is merely tales of the ancients.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p161/r1.anchor: واضح أن الآيات موجهه إلى تأييد نبوة المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام، تثبيت قلبه في مواجهة من يكذبونه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r1.claim: Khuluq concerns faculties perceived inwardly by insight, in contrast to created forms and shapes perceived by sight.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r1.anchor: وختص الخلق بالقوى المدركة بالبصيرة قال تعالى: {وَإِنَّكَ لَعَلَى خُلُقٍ عَظِيمٍ}

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r2.claim: Khalāq can mean the virtue a person acquires through character; ikhtilāq derives from creating or inventing, including fabricated speech.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r2.anchor: والخلاق: ما اكتسب الإنسان من الفضيلة بخلقه

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r3.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ interprets khalāq in al-Baqara as a share; in that verse he specifies a share of good.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r3.anchor: وتفسير "خلاق" بنصيب، هو معناه في آية البقرة عند الفراء

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r4.claim: Abū ʿUbayda also explains khalāq as a share in the cited verse from Āl ʿImrān.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r4.anchor: وأبي عبيدة في آية آل عمران

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r5.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib narrows the sense to a share of virtue a person has earned.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r5.anchor: وقيده الراغب بما اكتسب الإنسان من فضيلة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r6.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وسفيان
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī records Mujāhid, al-Suddī, and Sufyān as explaining khalāq as a share; he also reports other glosses and Ibn ʿAbbās’s “what sustains him.”
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r6.anchor: أنه النصيب، عن مجاهد والسدى وسفيان. والحجّة، عن قتادة، والدين، عن الحسن

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r7.claim: The author prefers “share,” its established Arabic meaning, supported by the Prophetic statement that God may strengthen the religion through people with no share in it.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r7.anchor: أنه النصيب، وذلك أنه معناه في كلام العرب. قال: ومنه قول النبي

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r8.claim: In the three Qur’anic occurrences, khalāq means a share of otherworldly recompense for deeds; the author compares “share” in Ghāfir and al-Shūrā and distinguishes inheritance usage in al-Nisāʾ.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p403/r8.anchor: وسياق الكلمة في آياتها الثلاث، صريح في أنه النصيب من الجزاء الأخروى على كسب الأعمال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p682/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p682/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p682/r1.claim: Al-Qalam's hammaz suits its focus on social conduct: it lists bad traits and commands nonobedience, with little outcome detail beyond branding; al-Humaza describes the end in detail.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p682/r1.anchor: أما في سورة القلم استخدام صيغة (همّاز) لأن الكلام في التعامل مع الناس وكل سورة القلم تتكلم عن التعامل مع الناس.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p307#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p307#2/r1.speaker: عائشة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p307#2/r1.claim: Asked to describe the Prophet's character, ʿĀʾisha says it was the Qurʾān.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p307#2/r1.anchor: فقلت نعم فقالت إن خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان القرآن

ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r1.claim: The Prophet’s character reaches a height no creature can attain; therefore he bears from others what even other resolute prophets could not.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r1.anchor: لا يدرك شأوه أحد من الخلق ولذلك تحتمل من جهتهم ما لا يحتمله أمثالك من أولي العزم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r2.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r2.claim: Asked by Sa‘d ibn Hisham about the Prophet’s character, Aisha replied that it was the Qur’an; reports are transmitted by Muslim, Abu Dawud, Ahmad, al-Darimi, Ibn Majah, and al-Nasa’i.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r2.anchor: وفي حديث مسلم وأبي داود والإمام أحمد والدارمي وابن ماجه والنسائي عن سعد بن هشام قال قلت لعائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها يا أم المؤمنين أنبئيني عن خلق رسول الله

ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r3.claim: One explanation of Aisha’s answer is that the Prophet embodied all the Qur’an’s virtues and refrained from the base manners it forbids, since he is its primary addressee.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r3.anchor: وأرادت بذلك على ما قيل أن ما فيه من المكارم كله كان فيه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وما فيه من الزجر عن سفساف الأخلاق كان منزجرا به

ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r4.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r4.claim: In a report cited from Abu al-Darda by Ibn al-Mundhir and others, Aisha says the Prophet’s character was the Qur’an: he approved what it approves and opposed what it condemns.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r4.anchor: كما في رواية ابن المنذر وغيره عن أبي الدرداء أنه سألها عن خلقه عليه الصلاة والسلام فقالت كان خلقه القرآن يرضى لرضاه ويسخط لسخطه

ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r5.speaker: المرصفي
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r5.claim: The mystic al-Mursafi says Aisha meant that the Prophet took on God’s attributes, but she avoided stating this explicitly out of reverence.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r5.anchor: وقال العارف بالله تعالى المرصفي أرادت بقولها كان خلقه القرآن تخلقه بأخلاق الله تعالى لكنها لم تصرح به تأدبا منها

ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r6.speaker: الكشف
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r6.claim: Al-Kashf sees an implicit indication in the description عظيم that the Prophet was characterized by God’s attributes.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r6.anchor: وفي الكشف أنه أدمج في هذه الجملة أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم متخلق بأخلاق الله عز وجل بقوله سبحانه عظيم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r7.claim: Some claim the verse hints that good morals and madness do not coexist: better character means greater distance from madness, while bad character is near it.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p25#2/r7.anchor: وزعم بعضهم أن في الآية رمزا إلى أن الأخلاق الحسنة مما لا تجامع الجنون وأنه كلما كان الإنسان أحسن أخلاقا كان أبعد عن الجنون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid understand the great character as the great religion of Islam, most beloved and approved by God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد: دين عظيم لا دين أحب إلي ولا أرضى عندي منه، وهو دين الإسلام.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r8.claim: Ḥasan says it means the manners taught by the Qurʾān.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r9.speaker: عائشة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r9.claim: When asked about the Prophet's character, ʿĀʾisha answered that his character was the Qurʾān.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r9.anchor: سئلت عائشة رضي الله عنها عن خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت: كان خلقه القرآن

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r10.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r10.claim: Qatāda explains that the Prophet obeyed God's commands and avoided His prohibitions: his character was what God commanded in the Qurʾān.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r10.anchor: وقال قتادة: هو ما كان يأتمر به من أمر الله وينتهي عنه من نهي الله، والمعنى إنك على الخلق الذي أمرك الله به في القرآن.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r11.claim: God called the Prophet's character great because he followed the instruction to take the pardon in 7:198.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r11.anchor: وقيل: سمى الله خلقه عظيما لأنه امتثل تأديب الله إياه بقوله: "خذ العفو" (الأعراف-198) الآية.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r12.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن جابر
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r12.claim: A report from Jābir says God sent the Prophet to perfect noble character traits and good actions; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r12.anchor: وروينا عن جابر أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إن الله بعثني لتمام مكارم الأخلاق، وتمام محاسن الأفعال"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r13.speaker: البراء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r13.claim: Al-Barāʾ says the Prophet was the best-looking and best-mannered person, neither unusually tall nor short; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r13.anchor: سمعت البراء يقول: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أحسن الناس وجها وأحسنهم خلقا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r14.speaker: أنس بن مالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r14.claim: Anas says he served the Prophet ten years without hearing a reproach or being asked why he acted or refrained; the Prophet had excellent character, exceptionally soft hands, and the sweetest scent.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p187#2/r14.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك قال: خدمت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عشر سنين فما قال لي أف قط [وما] (4) قال لشيء صنعته: لم صنعته؟ ولا لشيء تركته: لم تركته؟

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r5.claim: His character is great because he bears from his people what others like him could not bear.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r5.anchor: إذ تتحمل من قومك ما لا يتحمل أمثالك

BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r6.speaker: عائشة
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r6.claim: Asked about the Prophet's character, ʿĀʾisha said it was the Qur'an and asked whether the questioner had not read the opening of Sūrat al-Muʾminūn.
BAYDAWI-FULL:68:2-4/r6.anchor: وسئلت عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها عن خلقه صلى الله عليه وسلم

BINTSHATI:v2p45/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r3.claim: These assurances fortify the Prophet at the beginning of revelation, prepare him for the burden of conveying the message, and sustain him through the abuse of deniers.
BINTSHATI:v2p45/r3.anchor: فندرك عمق أثرها في تثبيت المصطفى وتقوية فؤاده، وتهيئته لما هو بسيل أن يحتمل من أعباء التبليغ

BINTSHATI:v2p50/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p50/r6.speaker: الإمام الطبري
BINTSHATI:v2p50/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits ʿĀʾisha's explanation of the Prophet's character: “His character was the Qur'an.”
BINTSHATI:v2p50/r6.anchor: نقل "الإمام الطبري" قول من فهموها بحديث السيدة عائشة رضي الله عنها، أنها سئلت عن خلق الرسول

BINTSHATI:v2p50/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p50/r7.speaker: عائشة
BINTSHATI:v2p50/r7.claim: ʿĀʾisha answers that the Prophet's character was the Qur'an; Bint al-Shati notes the chronological objection that this is an early Meccan verse, before much of the Qur'an's moral teaching had been revealed.
BINTSHATI:v2p50/r7.anchor: أنها سئلت عن خلق الرسول - صلى الله عليه وسلم - فقالت: كان خلقه القرآن. وقد يرد عليه أن الآية مكية مبكرة

BINTSHATI:v2p51/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r1.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r1.claim: Some interpret the phrase as “a great religion,” meaning Islam; Bint al-Shati rejects this because the Qur'an nowhere uses khuluq to mean religion.
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r1.anchor: وفسرها بعضهم بالدين: وإنك لعلى دين عظيم، وهو الإسلام.

BINTSHATI:v2p51/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r2.claim: The verse confirms God's knowledge of the Prophet's high character, recognized since boyhood and in his youth for trustworthiness, truthfulness, nobility, and chastity.
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r2.anchor: وإنما تؤكد الآية، ما علم الله من خلق نبيه المصطفى،

BINTSHATI:v2p51/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r3.speaker: أبو طالب
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r3.claim: At Muhammad and Khadīja's marriage, Abū Ṭālib praised Muhammad as unmatched among Quraysh youths in honor, nobility, merit, and intellect.
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r3.anchor: أو كما قال عمه أبو طالب في خطبة زواج محمد من خديجة بنت خويلد:

BINTSHATI:v2p51/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r4.speaker: خديجة
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r4.claim: Khadīja says God will not humiliate Muhammad because he keeps kinship ties, speaks truth, fulfills trusts, bears burdens, hosts guests, and helps in times of hardship.
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r4.anchor: وقالت أم المؤمنين الأولى، رضى الله عنها، في ليلة القدر:

BINTSHATI:v2p51/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r5.claim: Reports also say Quraysh called Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh “the trustworthy” before his prophetic mission.
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r5.anchor: ومعهاما تواتر به الخبر من لقب الأمين الذي أطلقته قريش على محمد بن عبد الله قبل المبعث.

BINTSHATI:v2p51/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r6.claim: This early revelation is God's testimony to the Prophet's great character, crowning his known virtues and strengthening him against arrogant deniers.
BINTSHATI:v2p51/r6.anchor: شهادة إلهية بعظمة خلق المصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام، تتوج ما كان معروفاً من مكارم أخلاقه

BINTSHATI:v2p71/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p71/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p71/r1.claim: The sūra’s closing words support the Prophet and link back to its opening, which likewise affirms his freedom from madness and his great character.
BINTSHATI:v2p71/r1.anchor: تأييداً للمصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام، يرتبط بما بدأت به السورة من مثل هذا التأييد الإلهي

BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r4.claim: Biqāʿī says denial precedes the quoted accusation to honor the Prophet and soften its impact; placing praise of his character before the accusation heightens that honor.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p96#2/r4.anchor: وتقدم الجواب بنفي قولهم والتنزيه عنه على حكاية قولهم ليكون أبلغ في إجلاله

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r5.claim: Although a rewarded person might have only modest reason, Muhammad stands at its highest rank; the opponents’ lack of happiness follows their lack of reason.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r5.anchor: بين أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم في أعلاها بقوله مؤكدا لما مضى

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r6.claim: The great character is Islam, the Qur’anic way Muhammad called people to: neither hardship bends him from it nor gifts turn him aside.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r6.anchor: وهو الإسلام الذي دعا إليه القرآن

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r7.speaker: عائشة
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r7.claim: ʿĀʾisha testified that the Prophet’s character was the Qur’an and that he moved or rested only according to its commands and prohibitions.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r7.anchor: بشهادة أعرف الناس به زوجه أم المؤمنين الصديقة عائشة بنت الصديق أبي بكر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r8.speaker: الواسطي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r8.claim: Al-Wāsiṭī says God displayed power in Jesus, efficacy in Āṣif, wrath in Moses’ staff, and divine qualities and noble character in Muhammad.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r9.claim: Khalq denotes outward form, while khuluq is inward form and is used for good character.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r9.anchor: أن الخلق والخلق صورتان : الخلق صور الظاهر

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r10.claim: Good character toward God is reverence; toward His rulings it is patience, gratitude, and willing obedience; toward people it is fairness and gracious companionship.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r10.anchor: فمع الله بالتعظيم والإجلال ومع حكمه بالصبر في الضراء والبأساء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r11.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r11.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said that character contains religion, from which submission, humility, self-sacrifice for God, and bearing hardship arise.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r11.anchor: روي عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r12.claim: Biqāʿī says Islam, the noblest religion, was given modesty as its finest character, and modesty gives life to the heart.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r12.anchor: أعطاه الله تعالى أقوى الأخلاق وأشرفها وهو الحياء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r13.claim: An unnamed report says every religion has a defining character and Islam’s is modesty; modesty is the life of the heart.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r13.anchor: أن لكل دين خلقا وخلق الإسلام الحياء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r14.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r14.claim: The Prophet embodied pardon, recognized good, and turning away from the ignorant; he forgave and kindly served even the man who pulled his cloak.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p97/r14.anchor: فكان صلى الله عليه وسلم يأخذ العفو ويأمر بالعرف ويعرض عن الجاهلين

DURR-FULL:v8p243/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r1.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r1.claim: ʿĀʾisha said that nobody had better character than the Prophet; when a Companion or family member called him, he answered “at your service,” and this occasioned the verse.
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r1.anchor: عن عائشة قالت: ما كان أحد أحسن خلقا من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ما دعاه أحد من أصحابه ولا من أهل بيته

DURR-FULL:v8p243/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r2.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r2.claim: In several answers about the Prophet's character, ʿĀʾisha said his character was the Qurʾān; he was pleased by what pleases it and angered by what angers it.
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r2.anchor: عن سعد بن هشام قال: أتيت عائشة فقلت يا أم المؤمنين: أخبرني بخلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت: كان خلقه القرآن

DURR-FULL:v8p243/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r3.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r3.claim: ʿĀʾisha described the Prophet as the best of people in character and said his character was the Qurʾān.
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r3.anchor: عن عبد الله بن شقيق العقيلي قال: أتيت عائشة فسألتها عن خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت: كان أحسن الناس خلقا

DURR-FULL:v8p243/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r4.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r4.claim: ʿĀʾisha said the Prophet was neither obscene nor loud in markets, did not answer evil with evil, and instead pardoned and forgave; al-Tirmidhī graded the report sound.
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r4.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله الجدلي قال: قلت لعائشة: كيف كان خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قالت: لم يكن فاحشا ولا متفحشا

DURR-FULL:v8p243/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r5.speaker: عائشة
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r5.claim: ʿĀʾisha told Syrian women that the Prophet's character was the Qurʾān and that he was shyer than secluded young women.
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r5.anchor: عن زينب بنت يزيد بن وسق قالت: كنت عند عائشة إذا جاءها نساء أهل الشام فقلن يا أم المؤمنين:

DURR-FULL:v8p243/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r6.speaker: عطية العوفي
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r6.claim: ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī explains the verse as the Prophet's adherence to Qurʾānic manners.
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r6.anchor: عن عطية العوفي في قوله: {وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم} قال: على أدب القرآن

DURR-FULL:v8p243/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās gives “the Qurʾān” as an explanation of the great character.
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس {وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم} قال: القرآن

DURR-FULL:v8p243/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also explains the great character as religion.
DURR-FULL:v8p243/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم} قال: الدين

DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r1.speaker: أبو مالك
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r1.claim: Abū Mālik explains the Prophet's great character as Islam.
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي مالك {وإنك لعلى خلق عظيم} قال: الإسلام

DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r2.speaker: ابن أبزى وسعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abzā and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr explain it as a great religion.
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبزى وسعيد بن جبير قالا: على دين عظيم

DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r3.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r3.claim: Anas said he served the Prophet for eleven years, and the Prophet never asked why he had or had not done something.
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r3.anchor: عن ثابت عن أنس قال: خدمت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إحدى عشرة سنة ما قال لي قط ألا فعلت هذا

DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r4.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r4.claim: Anas recalled that the Prophet never blamed him during his service from age eight; when another blamed him, the Prophet said to leave him, since what was decreed would happen.
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r4.anchor: عن أنس قال: خدمت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنا ابن ثمان سنين فما لامني على شيء يوما من الأيام

DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r5.speaker: ميمونة
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r5.claim: Maymūna recounted that the Prophet once returned after she locked him out at night; he swore her to open, denied visiting another wife, and explained he needed to relieve himself.
DURR-FULL:v8p243#2/r5.anchor: عن ميمونة قالت: خرج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذات ليلة من عندي فأغلقت دونه الباب فجاء يستفتح الباب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r7.claim: After the promise, God refutes the enemies again by confirming the Prophet’s tremendous character, the opposite of madness, with three emphases matching the previous sentence’s emphasis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r7.anchor: وبعد أن آنس نفس رسوله بالوعد عاد إلى تسفيه قول الأعداء فحقق أنه متلبس بخلق عظيم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r8.claim: خلق means the soul’s disposition and, when unqualified, is most often used for good character.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r8.anchor: والخلق : طباع النفس ، وأكثر إطلاقه على طباع الخير إذا لم يتبع بنعت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r9.claim: عظيم means high in rank, metaphorically borrowed from bodily bulk so commonly that the figurative use became nearly equivalent to the literal one.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r9.anchor: والعظيم : الرفيع القدر وهو مستعار من ضخامة الجسم ، وشاعت هذه الاستعارة حتى ساوت الحقيقة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r10.claim: على expresses metaphorical elevation in the sense of firm establishment, as in the cited descriptions of being upon guidance, truth, or a straight path.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p62/r10.anchor: و ( على ) للاستعلاء المجازي المراد به التمكن كقوله : أولئك على هدى من ربهم } ( البقرة : 5 ) ومنه قوله تعالى : { إنك على الحق المبين }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p64/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p64/r1.speaker: عائشة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p64/r1.claim: Asked about the Prophet’s character, ʿĀʾisha said it was the Quran: its virtues and noble qualities, and its prohibitions of their opposites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p64/r1.anchor: أنها سئلت عن خلق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقالت : كان خلقه القرآن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p64/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p64/r2.speaker: author
